action: Place the probe on the left flank. Angle the probe obliquely to align the footprint with the intercostal spaces (ribs).
interpretation: Establish an acoustic window ensuring visualization of all anatomical parts of the kidney.

action: Instruct patient: 'Take a nice deep breath in and hold'.
interpretation: Prepare to shift anatomical structures to optimize the scanning window.

action: Maintain probe position while the patient inspires.
interpretation: Observe the kidney displacing inferiorly, moving below the echogenic diaphragm and clearing overlying bowel gas.

action: Perform a complete sweep in the sagittal plane. Fan or slide from the anterior cortex of the kidney all the way through to the posterior cortex.
interpretation: Visualize the entire renal parenchyma in the longitudinal axis, ensuring no pathology is missed from front to back.
Change the plane of section to view the kidney in the transverse (short) axis.

action: Sweep the probe continuously from the upper pole of the kidney down to the lower pole.
interpretation: Scan through the full length of the kidney in cross-section to assess the entire organ.

action: Adjust the probe angle or slide to different intercostal windows to navigate around rib shadows. Specifically isolate the lower pole and the upper pole.
interpretation: Identify acoustic shadowing from the ribs obscuring the view and utilize alternative windows to visualize the poles clearly.
Obtain a high-quality, clear view of all renal structures, ensuring the image is free of artifacts.
